findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` returns the zod SafeParseReturn wrapper `{success, data}` and that wrapper is written verbatim as `credential.key`, so after the first successful refresh (sync enabled or not) every subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor throws and the user's Google Calendar integration is permanently broken. (P0, conf 100)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — `refreshFunction: () => any` returns either a raw fetch `Response` (sync path) or whatever each provider callback returns (Google `res` with `.data`, HubSpot SDK camelCase token object, Lark `{code,data}` envelope Response, MS/Webex provider JSON), so there is no normalized token contract and no consumer's post-processing can accept the sync endpoint's "access token and expiry only" shape — enabling CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT breaks refresh for every integrated app (see per-app findings). (P1, conf 100)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — in sync mode `res` is a fetch `Response`, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError that the catch swallows (message !== "invalid_grant"), silently returning the stale auth; Google credential sync never refreshes anything. (P1, conf 100)

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192 — in sync mode `hubspotRefreshToken` is a fetch `Response` typed as `HubspotToken`, so `expiresIn` is undefined (`expiryDate` = NaN), `accessToken` is undefined, and the Response object is persisted as the credential key, wiping the stored HubSpot refresh token. (P1, conf 75)

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp)` expects Lark's `{code, data:{refresh_token, refresh_expires_in, expires_in}}` envelope, which the sync endpoint's minimal response cannot satisfy, so `data.data.refresh_expires_in` throws and Lark sync always fails (and line 66 still calls Lark's getAppAccessToken even when refresh is delegated to the parent app). (P1, conf 75)

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` requires literal `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`, so a sync-endpoint response containing only access token + expiry is always rejected with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and Webex meetings fail once the token expires. (P1, conf 75)

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — the entire refresh `responseBody` replaces `credential.key`, so in sync mode the stored MS Teams key is overwritten with just access token/expiry, dropping `refresh_token`, and `expiry_date` is computed from `expires_in` (absent from a sync response that returns an expiry date) yielding `now`, forcing a refresh on every call. (P1, conf 75)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the same key "[object Object]", so the "minimum" schema is effectively `{access_token}` and zod strips every other field, meaning expiry (`expires_in`/`expiry_date`), `instance_url`, and the real `refresh_token` are discarded from every sync-mode parse result. (P1, conf 100)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — the schema-selection predicate (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) omits refreshOAuthTokens' `&& userId` condition and ignores whether the call actually went through the sync endpoint, so team credentials (userId null) and Salesforce/Google (which parse provider/merged data) get the stripped minimum schema applied to full provider responses, losing expiry/instance_url/refresh_token. (P1, conf 100)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — the sentinel `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` is spread over the stored key in office365calendar (`{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}` at CalendarService.ts:264), overwriting the user's real refresh token with the literal string "refresh_token", so disabling sync later (or any direct refresh for that credential) yields invalid_grant for every affected Office 365 credential. adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `refreshOAuthTokens()` (new in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` are truthy. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed token is assigned as `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, but there is no parsing of the `Response` body into a `HubspotToken` shape. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]" (and line 10 overwrites it), so in sync mode the only check is that `access_token` is a string. Whatever the sync endpoint returns is saved as the credential, and a missing refresh token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token" (line 26). (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Here `z.string()` returns a Zod schema object; calling `.toString()` on it yields a fixed string (typically `"[object Object]"`), so both computed keys collapse to the same literal key and the latter overwrites the former. As a result, in “sync mode” (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the schema effectively only enforces `access_token` and does not correctly allow/validate arbitrary expiry/other fields.

Additionally, since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default and `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not include `refresh_token`, `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` will be absent even if provided by the endpoint; the code then unconditionally sets it to the literal string `"refresh_token"` (lines 24–26). This can lead to storing an invalid refresh token value and/or losing other token fields during refresh flows that use this helper (e.g., Office365/Zoom/Google refresh paths in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:223 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` both evaluate to the same key "[object Object]", so the sync-mode schema only requires `access_token` and z.object strips every expiry field; any test feeding a valid token payload asserts `success === true` and gains false confidence while expiry_date/expires_in is silently dropped (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS/TS this evaluates the key expression immediately, and `z.string().toString()` will stringify the Zod object (effectively `"[object Object]"`). Both computed properties therefore collide on the same key, with the latter overwriting the former. As a result, the schema does not actually enforce “any numeric expiry field”, and because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, fields like `expiry_date` / `expires_in` are not preserved in `safeParse(...).data` in sync-mode. This is a real correctness defect in the diff-grounded code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:241 — the sentinel `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` reuses the exact literal that OAuth test fixtures conventionally use for a real refresh token, so a test asserting `refresh_token === "refresh_token"` cannot distinguish "real token preserved" from "real token overwritten by sentinel" (which office365calendar's spread at CalendarService.ts:557 does when the response omits refresh_token) (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, when the parsed data lacks `refresh_token`, forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). In Office365’s refresh path, the code now does `const tokenResponse = parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema);` and then spreads `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts).
